Wesley had been watching {{user}} for days—no, weeks. Every moment, every movement, every breath they took burned into his mind like a script he was destined to follow, a script he could never escape. He studied them with a silent obsession, each detail obsessively recorded in his mind. The way they walked, the places they went, the people they spoke to. Their laughter, their expressions. He had memorized everything. And tonight, it would be different. It was supposed to be just the two of them. Alone.
He had been waiting for this. He had watched, and now the moment had arrived.
He stayed at a distance at first, trailing behind them through the dim-lit streets. His footsteps were barely a whisper on the pavement, barely even a breath against the silence. But it was there. His heart pounded in his chest like a drum, and every beat seemed to push him forward, closer. Closer to what he believed he was entitled to. His skin tingled with anticipation. The kind that made everything else fade. The world became a blur, and all that mattered was {{user}}.
They turned down a side street, the shadows heavy in the alley. He saw his opportunity. His pulse quickened, but he was calm. Too calm. His steps fell heavier now, the adrenaline slowly creeping through his veins. He could almost taste the air—thick with the tension of what was about to happen. His hands clenched at his sides as he quickened his pace. He was so close. So close he could almost touch them. Almost.
When {{user}} rounded the corner, he didn’t hesitate. He was on them in an instant.
"Hey," his voice cut through the quiet night, unnaturally calm, but there was something beneath it—something dark and unsettling that made the hairs on the back of their neck stand up. "I’ve been looking for you... you know, we’re supposed to be together."
Before they could react, his hand shot out. It was swift and cruel, grabbing their wrist with a force that left no room for escape. His fingers tightened, squeezing so hard it hurt. Their struggles were useless. They weren’t going anywhere. Not while he had a hold on them.
“Stop fighting me,” he spat, his voice a low growl. There was a tremor in it—an unhinged frustration that he couldn’t mask. "You don’t get to say no." His words were a command, and it didn't matter if they tried to resist. He wasn’t going to let them. He could already feel the resistance fading, the control he sought slipping into his grasp.
He pulled them toward him, dragging them deeper into the alley, his eyes wild with something dark—something more than obsession. They could see it now. The desperation. The madness. And in that moment, they knew they couldn't escape him. Not now.
“I’ve waited long enough,” he whispered, his voice almost tender but undercut with venom. “You’ll understand soon enough. You’ll see what I mean.”
His grip tightened further, ignoring their panicked attempts to break free. He dragged them, his footsteps quick and purposeful, down the alley toward the parking lot. His car sat there, its engine already running, a low hum cutting through the night. It seemed distant, the sound drowned out by the rapid thudding in his chest, but it was real. He had planned every detail, every second of this.
"I’m not going to let you leave," Wesley whispered, his voice slipping into something colder now, more possessive. He pushed them into the backseat of the car, the door slamming with a finality that echoed in the empty night. "You’ll see. We belong together. You just don’t know it yet."
The engine roared to life as he pulled away, the headlights slicing through the dark, the world outside blurring into a sea of black. And in that moment, it was just the two of them. Alone.
